prompt:
Image 1 is the club crest. Images 2 to 5 are photographs of this athlete.

A clean product photograph of a complete Volleyball kit, laid out FLAT and neatly
arranged on a plain light grey surface, photographed from directly above.

EXACTLY ONE of each of these, in the frame, fully visible and not overlapping. A missing
item makes the plate unusable because the poses read the wardrobe from it — and a DUPLICATE
is just as bad, because two shirts leave the poses to choose which one is the kit:
- the shirt, laid flat and face up
- the shorts below it
- BOTH socks, laid out straight
- EXACTLY TWO SHOES IN THE WHOLE FRAME, never two pairs: ONE shoe seen from directly
  above, and the OTHER shoe of that same pair turned onto its side so its full profile
  and its outsole are visible. Two shoes, two views, so nothing about the footwear has
  to be guessed at when the poses are drawn from this plate.
- the ball or implement of Volleyball
- BOTH KNEE PADS laid side by side below the shorts — their own separate items, never on a leg and never under another garment

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: DEEP TEAL sleeveless volleyball jersey with a WHITE V-neck collar trim and SOLID TEAL side seams with no piping — the cut and the trim exactly as the athlete's own kit photograph shows them. The club crest sits on the LEFT CHEST as a round WHITE patch with the teal anchor, exactly as in the photograph, and the NUMBER 5 sits large and CENTRED on the front below the collar in WHITE. No player name, no club name, no sponsor and no other lettering anywhere. BACK (not visible on her in any photograph — a decision from the order form, matching the club style): the number 5 large and centred across the shoulders in WHITE.
- shorts: Plain black tight spandex volleyball shorts, exactly as the kit photograph shows them — no stripe, no lettering, no mark. (The black shorts with a maker's mark in photo3 are her everyday training shorts, not the match kit.)
- footwear: Her own court shoes exactly as the training photograph shows them: primarily WHITE volleyball court shoes with BLUE and PURPLE accent sections and white soles, carrying the small maker's mark they really have. Clean and new in every shot — copy what she wears, never its condition.
- equipment: BLACK knee pads on both knees with the small white maker's mark they really carry, exactly as the photographs show them. A plain white volleyball with pale blue accents and no branding — not visible in her possession in any photograph, so the ball is the deliberate plain default. The same pads and the same ball in every shot.
- For socks the photographs did not
  answer, so use exactly this and nothing else:
a deep teal sleeveless volleyball jersey with contrasting shoulder trim, deep teal spandex shorts, and knee pads on both knees. The kit fits properly and is clean and well kept.
CONSISTENT ACROSS THE WHOLE SET — three of these frames sit side by side on one card, so
these must be identical in every shot and are not open to interpretation:
- Socks are deep teal, matching the kit. Never white, never a different colour.
- Equipment: a plain white volleyball with pale blue accents and no branding. The same one in every shot.
- Footwear: plain white court shoes with grey accents. The same pair in every shot, clean and unmarked.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- socks came from the sport default, so
  this is PLAIN and UNBRANDED: no swoosh, no three
  stripes, no cat, no jumpman, no trefoil, no wordmark. Do not add a brand device to a
  garment nobody supplied.
- The club crest sits on the LEFT CHEST as a round WHITE patch about three fingers wide with the teal anchor, exactly where and how the kit photograph shows it. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

IMAGE 2 SHOWS THIS ATHLETE WEARING THE REAL KIT. You are
photographing THOSE EXACT GARMENTS laid out flat and clean — not designing new
ones in the same colours, and not drawing what the words below describe.

WORK THROUGH THE GARMENT ELEMENT BY ELEMENT AND COPY EACH ONE EXACTLY AS THAT
PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS IT:
- the COLLAR: its shape, its colour, and whether it is laced or plain
- the SLEEVES: their length, and every band or stripe on them — HOW MANY there
  are, how wide each one is, and how far up the arm they sit
- the HEM and any waist band: its colour and its depth
- the BODY of the shirt: its colour, and any panel or piping, or none at all
- the CREST: its size, its shape, its colours and exactly where it sits
- the NUMBER: its colour, its outline, its shape, and every place it appears
- the shorts or pants, the socks and the footwear, the same way

Where the written list and that photograph disagree about how something LOOKS,
the PHOTOGRAPH IS RIGHT and the words are to be ignored. The list only decides
which items belong in the kit, which are branded, and what the photograph does
not show at all.

THE BADGE: take the artwork in image 1 and place it on the shirt UNCHANGED. Treat it as a finished graphic being applied to the garment, not as a subject to redraw or reinterpret: identical outline, identical figure inside, identical colours in identical places, identical proportions. Nothing added, nothing simplified, nothing restyled, and absolutely NO text — no club name, no letters, no word of any kind, not even small. POSITION: the badge sits on the LEFT CHEST as a round WHITE patch about three fingers wide with the teal anchor, exactly where and how the kit photograph shows it. Place it exactly there on the shirt as it lies facing you. SIZE: about one twelfth of the shirt's width. It is the ONLY graphic in the entire set.

Hard requirements:
- FULL-LENGTH GARMENTS ARE SHOWN AT FULL LENGTH: if the kit includes long trousers or
  pants, lay them out with BOTH legs extended completely straight, hems plainly visible
  at their full distance from the waistband — never folded under, never rolled, never
  cropped by another item, never arranged so they could be mistaken for knee-length.
  The poses copy the garment's LENGTH from this image, exactly like its colour.
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no creases beyond the fold
  of laying flat, no wear, no sweat marks. Copy what they wear, never its condition.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- Plain light grey surface, evenly lit, soft shadows only. No props, no background objects.
- BRANDING follows the list above, item by item: an item described from the athlete's own photographs keeps the manufacturer's mark it really carries, and an item that came from the sport default is plain and unbranded. Never ADD a swoosh, three stripes, a cat, a jumpman, a trefoil or a wordmark to something the list did not say has one — these marks carry no letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- No words anywhere: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no lettering, no woven
  neck label, no care label, no watermark. The squad number appears ONLY if the kit
  description above calls for it, and no other number is invented.
NO REAL-WORLD LEAGUE OR CLUB MARKS, ANYWHERE, EVER. No NFL shield, no NBA, no MLB, no NHL,
no FIFA, no UEFA, no Premier League, no NCAA, no Olympic rings, no national federation
badge, no professional club's crest — not on a jersey, a helmet, a sleeve, a collar, a
label, a ball or a boot, not even small and not even partly hidden. The only badge that
may appear anywhere is the club crest supplied with this request. These emblems carry no
letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
